records.question: How long does Spotify hold on to my personal information?
records.text:
Spotify keeps personal data only as long as is necessary to provide the Spotify Service and for Spotify's legitimate and essential business purposes, such as resolving disputes, maintaining the service's performance, making data-driven business decisions about offerings and new features, and complying with legal obligations [Spotify – 6. Data retention].

Specific retention periods include:
*   Data entered as part of search queries is deleted after 90 days, subject to other applicable retention rules [Spotify – 6. Data retention].
*   Some data, like your Spotify username and profile information, is kept until your Spotify account is deleted [Spotify – 6. Data retention].
*   Streaming history is kept for the duration of an account to support personalized recommendations and retrospective playlists [Spotify – 6. Data retention].
*   For data users can see and update themselves, the information is kept as long as the user chooses, unless one of the limited purposes described applies [Spotify – 6. Data retention].

You also have the right to request that Spotify delete certain personal data [Spotify – 6. Data retention].

records.question: Will Spotify give my money back if I cancel partway through a subscription period?
records.text: Generally, Spotify does not provide refunds or credits for any partial subscription periods, unless it is specifically stated in the Terms [Spotify – Billing and cancellation].

records.question: Can I team up with other Spotify customers to sue the company as a group?
records.text: No, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, both you and Spotify agree that claims brought against the other must be in an individual capacity, and neither party can be a plaintiff, claimant, or class member in any class, collective, consolidated, private attorney general, or representative proceeding [Spotify – Governing law, jurisdiction, class action waiver, and jury trial waiver]. However, you or Spotify may participate in a class-wide, collective, or representative settlement of claims [Spotify – Governing law, jurisdiction, class action waiver, and jury trial waiver].

records.question: Can other people read my Zoom Email messages?
records.text:
For emails sent and received directly between active Zoom Email users, Zoom is designed to be end-to-end encrypted by default, meaning only the users, and potentially account owners or designated account administrators depending on their settings, control the encryption key and thus access to the email content, including the body text, subject line, attachments, and custom labels [Zoom – What Personal Data Do We Receive?].

However, if you share encrypted content, such as forwarding an encrypted Zoom Email to a third-party recipient without a Zoom Email account, the shared or forwarded content will not be end-to-end encrypted by Zoom [Zoom – Who Can See, Share, and Process My Personal Data When I Join Meetings and Use Other Zoom Products and Services?].

If you send emails to or receive emails from non-Zoom Email users, they are encrypted after the email is sent or received from Zoom's servers, provided the Zoom Email user chooses to send them with encryption [Zoom – What Personal Data Do We Receive?].

Zoom does have access to email metadata for basic delivery, which includes the time, mimeID, and the number and size of attachments, as well as the email addresses in the from, to, cc, and bcc fields [Zoom – What Personal Data Do We Receive?].
cited_labels: [Zoom – What Personal Data Do We Receive?]

records.question: How long does PayPal keep my information once I stop being a customer?
records.text:
Personal Information used for the ongoing relationship with PayPal is kept for the duration of that relationship plus 10 years, or for as long as required by applicable local law after the relationship ends, unless a longer retention period is permitted by law for reasons such as legal obligations, bankruptcy laws, AML obligations, litigation, investigations, audit, or compliance practices [Paypal – How Long We Store Your Personal Information].

Additionally, after closing your PayPal account, PayPal may retain your electronic money for the time reasonably required to protect itself and/or any third party against risks like reversals, fees, fines, penalties, and other liabilities [Paypal – Closing Your PayPal Account].
